title: Expose durable completed-job history with prompt metadata
description:
Add a stable JSON command (`cmfy jobs list --json`, or a clearly documented equivalent) that enumerates queued, running, failed, cancelled, and completed Comfy jobs across process restarts. Each record must retain the original prompt identity and submission metadata needed by clients: prompt ID, workflow name/path or stable workflow identity, user prompt, dimensions and other explicit submission parameters, status, submitted/updated timestamps, and output descriptors/paths when available.

The durable authority must live in cmfy/ComfyUI-accessible state rather than frontend localStorage or one client App's private index. Existing `job status`, `job wait`, `job cancel`, and `queue` behavior must remain compatible. JSON output must be machine-only and bounded/paginatable; human progress belongs on stderr. Do not expose credentials or server configuration.

Positive proof:
1. Add tests that submit at least two mocked jobs with distinct prompts/workflows.
2. Recreate the command/service object to simulate a new process, then list history and recover both exact prompts and statuses.
3. Transition one job through completion with output metadata and one through cancellation/failure; prove list filtering/order/pagination deterministically.
4. Prove `--json` contains one valid JSON value with no prose framing.
5. Run Go formatting, focused tests, full `go test ./...`, and relevant CLI smoke tests.
6. Update README/help with schema, durability location, ordering, bounds, and compatibility behavior.

title: run_cmd uses Load() instead of LoadWithVars(), ignoring workflow variable defaults
description: run_cmd.go line 123 calls workflow.Load() which does not parse the 'variables' section from workflow JSON files. This means: (1) Variable defaults defined in the workflow are never applied. (2) The 'variables' block is sent to ComfyUI as a node, causing 'missing_node_type' error for node ID '#variables'. Fix: Change workflow.Load() to workflow.LoadWithVars() in run_cmd.go and pass varDefaults to ApplyVarsWithDefaults() instead of ApplyVars().

title: Bug: Async mode doesn't download images to output_dir
description:
When running cmfy workflows in async mode (--async), the workflow executes successfully on the ComfyUI server but the generated images are NOT downloaded to the configured output folder.

## Reproduction

1. Sync mode (works):
   ./cmfy run -w Movie_Madness --prompt "test" --width 1024 --height 768 --steps 28
   → Saves to outputs/cmfy_00044_.png ✅

2. Async mode (broken):
   ./cmfy run -w Movie_Madness --prompt "test" --width 1024 --height 768 --steps 28 --async
   → Returns prompt_id, job completes, but NO file in outputs/ ❌

## Investigation

ComfyUI server history shows the image was generated:
```json
{
  "outputs": {
    "9": {
      "images": [{"filename": "cmfy_00045_.png", "subfolder": "", "type": "output"}]
    }
  }
}
```

But cmfy never fetches it from the /view endpoint.

## Expected

Both sync and async modes should save images to output_dir.

## Impact

Async mode is unusable for production since users can't retrieve their generated images.

## Suggested Fix

After async job completes, cmfy should:
1. Get output filenames from /history/<prompt_id>
2. Download each image via /view?filename=... endpoint
3. Save to output_dir

title: ComfyUI export plugin should emit 'variables' block with defaults
description: The ComfyUI-cmfy-export plugin should include a 'variables' section in the exported JSON with default values taken from the current workflow values. This way workflows are self-documenting and cmfy can use the defaults when flags are not provided. Depends on trx-8b2t (LoadWithVars fix) to work correctly.

title: SaveVideo output not downloaded - cmfy only checks 'images' key
description: When a workflow uses SaveVideo, ComfyUI returns output with both 'images' (containing .mp4 files) and 'animated' keys. The run_cmd output download loop correctly iterates om['images'], but reports 'no images saved' when the video was actually generated on the server. This may be due to the /view endpoint not serving video files correctly, or a timing issue with the history API. Need to investigate why SaveVideo outputs appear in /api/history but cmfy reports 0 saved files.

title: Harden output downloads against path escape and unbounded bodies
description:
`downloadOutputsFromMap` trusts ComfyUI-controlled `filename` and writes `filepath.Join(cfg.OutputDir, filename)`. A malicious or compromised server can return `../outside` or an absolute path and escape the configured output root. `Client.View` also buffers an unbounded response into memory, and downloads are written directly to the final path, leaving partial files on failure.

Fix the root cause at a shared output-materialization seam: validate and canonicalize every server output descriptor, preserve only safe relative subfolders when explicitly supported, prove the destination remains beneath the canonical output root, reject symlinks/escapes, enforce configurable per-file and aggregate response limits, stream to a same-directory temporary file, fsync/close as appropriate, and atomically rename. Define deterministic collision behavior; never silently overwrite an unrelated file. Keep JSON stdout machine-clean and diagnostics on stderr.

Positive proof:
1. httptest responses containing `../escape`, absolute paths, separator variants, and symlink destinations cannot create/modify anything outside the temp output root.
2. Oversized and interrupted responses fail without retaining a partial final file.
3. Valid image/video/audio descriptors save successfully with deterministic collision handling.
4. Tests cover duplicate filenames from different subfolders/nodes.
5. Run gofmt, go vet ./..., go test ./..., and a CLI download smoke test.

title: Provide one stable machine-output contract across cmfy commands
description:
Make every automation-relevant command support a consistent global machine contract: `--json` emits exactly one bounded JSON value on stdout, `--jsonl`/`watch` emits documented framed events where applicable, and all progress/warnings/human diagnostics go to stderr. Add `--quiet` and stable exit/error codes. In particular, `run --async` must return a structured submission record rather than requiring clients to scrape `Prompt ID:`, and `job wait --json --download` must not interleave `Saved:` or `Workflow completed` prose before its JSON result.

Keep one typed internal result model shared by human and machine renderers instead of branching business logic. Document versioned schemas and compatibility policy.

Positive proof:
1. Table-driven CLI tests cover run, batch, queue, job status/wait/cancel, workflows list/show/inspect, and server ping.
2. Success and failure stdout always parse according to the selected framing; stderr may contain progress but no secrets.
3. Existing human output remains useful when machine mode is absent.
4. Oqto Comfy Studio bridge can delete prompt-ID/prose extraction code and consume structured output directly.
5. Run gofmt, go vet ./..., go test ./..., and shell framing tests.

title: cmfy as a secure durable agent-grade ComfyUI execution substrate
description:
Implement the approved cmfy roadmap as one shared deterministic substrate for terminal users, agents, and Oqto Apps: safe bounded transport and output materialization; a deep Resolve→Plan→Submit→Observe→Collect engine; durable XDG/configurable job history and provenance; stable JSON/JSONL contracts; workflow contracts and preflight; WebSocket progress with fallback; idempotency, caching, resumability, cancellation outcomes, batch controls, server profiles, comprehensive tests, and migration of Comfy Studio away from private parsing/history workarounds.

The core must encode mechanism, not aesthetic or prompt judgment. Every surface shares the same typed substrate. Credentials remain outside history and sandbox payloads. All output/state paths are containment-checked. Existing human CLI behavior remains compatible unless an explicitly documented correction is required.

Positive proof is the union of child issue gates plus: gofmt, go vet ./..., go test ./..., deterministic CLI framing smokes, restart/concurrency tests, hostile HTTP/path tests, and a live Oqto Comfy Studio generation/reopen trace using canonical cmfy jobs.

title: Extract shared execution engine
description: Create typed Resolve→Plan→Submit→Observe→Collect interfaces used by run, aliases, batch, jobs, and external adapters. Remove duplicated orchestration from Cobra handlers and prove equivalent behavior through unit and command tests.

title: Add deterministic workflow contracts and preflight
description: Add JSON describe/validate/plan commands exposing workflow digest, required variables/assets, unresolved placeholders, output kinds, mapped parameters, and server dependency gaps. Fail loud; do not guess or select workflows.

title: Add WebSocket job events with polling fallback
description: Consume ComfyUI WebSocket execution/progress/preview events, expose bounded versioned JSONL watch events, resume via job state, and fall back to polling when unavailable. Test reconnect, malformed frames, and terminal states.

title: Add idempotent submissions, caching, resumable collection, and batch controls
description: Add request IDs with deduplication, content-hash upload reuse, resumable collision-safe output collection, explicit cancellation outcomes, bounded batch concurrency/queue policy, and deterministic retry semantics.

title: Add server profiles and capability inspection
description: Add named server profiles and machine-readable server inspection for endpoints, node/model inventory, and supported features. Keep credentials external and never persist URL credentials or headers in history.

title: Build comprehensive cmfy integration and CLI contract tests
description: Cover comfy client, engine, state migrations/restarts/concurrency, output containment, command framing, workflow contracts, events, cancellation, batch controls, and server profiles with httptest and filesystem fixtures.

title: Migrate Oqto Comfy Studio to canonical cmfy contracts
description: After cmfy contracts land, replace App-side prompt-ID scraping, job JSON ownership, graph filtering, and polling workarounds with pinned canonical cmfy JSON/JSONL operations; preserve Oqto authorization and workspace isolation and prove desktop/mobile reopen behavior.
